documents.title: M2023.11.28 Motion to Recommend Adoption of AI Policy
documents.stance_why: The motion has instructors "set their own policies" in their courses, but also states that students are "prohibited" from using generative AI "unless given explicit permission". Because the permission rests on each instructor, it sets no tiers and hands the decision to instructors. It does set a university-wide ban-by-default and a disclosure rule, so restrict is the other candidate, but the instructor discretion sentence comes first and frames the whole policy.
documents.summary: A Faculty Senate motion recommending a university-wide AI policy. Instructors set their own course rules and put them in the syllabus. Unless an instructor gives explicit permission, students may not use generative AI for exams or assignments. Notable AI use must be acknowledged, and students who are unsure must ask. The PDF leaves the vote blank, so adoption is not confirmed.

units.why: The sentence gives each instructor "the discretion to set their own policies", so the university sets no single rule and delegates; this is actor instructor, phase before-course (policy design), modality may, type P04 (per-instructor rule).
units.anchor: instructors have the discretion to set their own policies

units.why: "Such guidelines should be detailed in the course syllabi and clearly conveyed to students" tells instructors to put AI expectations in the syllabus; actor instructor, phase course-start, modality should, type P09.
units.anchor: Such guidelines should be detailed in the course syllabi and clearly conveyed to

units.why: "instructors should report impermissible use of AI to the Office of Student Accountability" sets a reporting step after suspected misuse; actor instructor, phase when-misuse, modality should. P81 (formal reporting procedure) fits better than P36 because the point is the reporting step, not the classification.
units.policy: Instructors should report impermissible use of AI to the Office of Student Accountability, as in all instances of academic misconduct.

units.why: "Students are prohibited from employing generative AI tools to complete exams or assignments ... unless given explicit permission" bans AI by default and allows it only with instructor permission; actor student, phase during-work, modality must-not, type P01 (default ban on graded work). P06 is about a silent syllabus, which this does not address.
units.anchor: Students are prohibited from employing generative AI tools to complete exams or assignments
units.policy: Students are prohibited from employing generative AI tools to complete exams or assignments (including papers, projects, computer programs, oral presentations, or other course requirements), unless given explicit permission from their course instructor.
units.fit_note: The ban is conditional on explicit instructor permission and lists computer programs among covered work; the type covers only the default ban.

units.why: "Unauthorized use of generative AI is treated as use of unauthorized assistance from another individual" classifies misuse as an integrity violation and equates AI with another person; actor all, phase when-misuse, modality informs. P36 (misconduct) chosen over P45 because the passage is about how violations are classified.
units.anchor: generative AI is treated as use of unauthorized assistance from another individual.

units.why: "all notable uses of generative AI should be acknowledged by the student in writing or via citation at the time of assignment submission" requires disclosure "Regardless of the course AI policy"; actor student, phase during-work, modality should, type P24.
units.anchor: all notable uses of generative AI should be acknowledged by the student in writing
units.policy: Regardless of the course AI policy, all notable uses of generative AI should be acknowledged by the student in writing or via citation at the time of assignment submission.

units.why: "when unsure, students should err on the side of full disclosure" is a separate rule for uncertain cases that pushes toward more disclosure; actor student, phase during-work, modality should. P24 is the nearest type; P10 is about asking, which the next sentence covers.
units.anchor: when unsure, students should err on the side of full disclosure
units.fit_note: Sets a lean-toward-more-disclosure rule when the student is unsure; the type does not capture that.

units.why: "it is their responsibility to seek clarification from their instructors prior to its use" tells students unsure about permissibility to ask first; actor student, phase course-start, modality must, type P10.
units.anchor: it is their responsibility to seek clarification from their instructors

units.policy: If students are unsure of the permissibility of the use of generative AI in a specific course context, it is their responsibility to seek clarification from their instructors prior to its use.

units.why: "Recognizing both the diverse potential benefits and challenges of generative AI across academic areas" gives the reason for delegating to instructors; it names benefits and challenges without a rule. Actor all, phase general, modality informs. P87 is the nearest type but it also names challenges.
units.anchor: Recognizing both the diverse potential benefits and challenges of generative AI
units.fit_note: Names challenges as well as benefits, and ties them to the choice to delegate to instructors.

units.why: The Whereas clauses say a Faculty Senate committee formed a taskforce "charged with researching this issue, writing a report, and developing a policy"; this describes how the policy was made. Actor admin, phase before-course, modality informs, type P84.
units.anchor: developing a policy on the use of AI for the University
units.policy: The Faculty Senate Academic Policies Committee created a taskforce charged with researching AI use, writing a report, and developing a policy on the use of AI for the University.

units.why: "The Faculty Senate recommends that the University adopt the following AI policy" states the policy is a recommendation, with adoption pending; this describes the policy-making process and status. Actor admin, phase before-course, modality informs, type P84.
units.anchor: The Faculty Senate recommends that the University adopt the following AI policy
